The vandalism comes amidst growing backlash against AI and the data centers that empower its growth. Scores of people have been arrested in the United States after protesting or defying municipal leaders during local meetings. The temperature is rising to such a level that the social risk to AI data center development in the US alone threatened some $130 billion worth of investments as of mid-August. The vandalism in Montreal is just a microcosm of that popular anti-AI sentiment — showing that if people continue to be ignored by their elected officials, they’re not afraid to take matters into their own hands. candidates.title: “Slop Grenades”: Shopify CEO Who Pushed Staff to Use AI Is Now Horrified by What He’s Wrought
candidates.raw_excerpt: Shopify CEO Tobias Lütke is getting a first-hand look at the AI-workplace revolution, and it isn’t a pretty sight. New reporting by Fortune revealed the disastrous results of Shopify’s all-out scramble to embrace AI nearly a year ago. After telling workers that using AI tools is a “baseline expectation” in the workplace, Lütke is now changing his tune as workers spew out AI-generated emails, memos, and code without double-checking it beforehand. “We call those ‘slop grenades’ that people toss at each other,” Lütke said in an interview on the Knowledge Project podcast . “That’s definitely a bad thing.” The CEO further explained that the initiative incentivized workers to “go nuts” on AI, leading to a deluge of AI generated slop. “You don’t really read it, and now it has to be reviewed by your colleagues, and they are like, ‘this doesn’t look right,'” he complained. “You’re just letting AI do the work for you.” As ironic as it may be for the once-AI-happy Shopify exec, he’s far from alone. An April survey of 1,150 office workers found that 40 percent had encountered a phenomenon known as “workslop,” or AI-generated content that looks professional on the surface but lacks any actual substance. Estimates found workers already waste 3.4 hours a month cleaning up the AI schlock, amounting to a monthly loss of $8.1 million for a workplace with 10,000 employees. Another survey from earlier in September found that negative sentiments around AI in workplace have exploded over the past few years, with the majority of workers now expressing negative attitudes toward the tech. Whatever way you slice it, it’s clear that AI is not a catch-all for workplace productivity — an obnoxious lesson Shopify’s Lütke had to learn the hard way. candidates.raw_excerpt: Image: Though the spiral galaxy in this new image  by the NASA/ESA  Hubble Space Telescope  seems serene, it hides a chaotic secret. This galaxy is NGC 4698, and it lies about 55 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo. It’s one of over one thousand galaxies in the Virgo Cluster, the nearest large cluster of galaxies bound together by gravity. As a spiral galaxy similar to our own Milky Way galaxy, NGC 4698 has spiral arms that curl around within a thin disc of stars, gas and dust. Its centre is dominated by a galactic bulge. The diffuse off-white glow of the galaxy’s bulge comes from stars smaller, older, and cooler than the massive blue stars that dot the galaxy’s outer disc. These tightly packed stars orbit a supermassive black hole containing millions of times the Sun’s mass. Scientists have found signs that this black hole is actively growing, drawing gas inward with its gravitational pull. With a flat, starry disc and diffusely glowing centre, NGC 4698 looks a lot like a typical spiral galaxy — but this galaxy is far from normal. NGC 4698 is one of only a few known spiral galaxies with a bulge that extends out from the disc at a right angle. The elongation is faintly visible in this Hubble image, which shows the ghostly glow of the starry bulge peeking above and below the dusty disc. What’s more, the stars and gas nearest the galaxy’s centre rotate perpendicular to the rest of the disc. What could cause a galaxy to be so out of sync? Astronomers have found that the culprit likely lies outside the galaxy. If NGC 4698 funneled in gas from an outside source, the newly collected gas could have formed a disc of gas and stars in the galaxy’s centre, at an angle relative to the rest of the disc. candidates.raw_excerpt: Vantor has selected EnduroSat and CACI to provide the satellite bus and payloads for its upcoming Pulse fleet, the company’s move into the smallsat imaging market. Vantor also said that Pulse satellites can accommodate different types of sensors, including electro-optical and radio-frequency payloads. Payloads can be adapted for sovereign missions for U.S. and allied nations. Vantor is also planning for its next-generation of high-resolution satellites. The company expects to launch two Vantage satellites as early as 2029 which will feature a larger bus and 20-centimeter-class resolution. “We’re designing the [Pulse] fleet to support different sensor types over time and feed that data into Tensorglobe, where it can be brought together with AI and other data sources. Combined with our higher-resolution satellites, that gives customers both the persistence to see change and the detail to understand what matters,” Matt Jenkins, Vantor chief space systems officer said in a release.
